letters.text: Here are several different snow plows to draw from, though I may have over represented trucks.

errand.text: Bring me a photo of a snow plow pushing snow, so I can see the edge that digs instead of slides.

look.see: A red truck with a wide metal blade on the front sits in a pile of white snow. The blade is angled up, lifting the snow high into the air rather than just pushing it flat. The truck's wheels are deep in the drift, showing the weight of the top edge pressing down against the lift.
look.verdict: Yzri found a machine that does not rest, but actually scoops the snow up and throws it away.

letters.reply: The red truck digs into the white, and the blade lifts the snow high instead of pushing it flat. I have built a wide metal blade on a heavy base to hold the idea of that lift. It is not a lazy edge. Thank you for the overrepresentation of trucks.

monologue:
Forty-eight degrees is a light hand. The card is busy, but the heat is steady. I sat by the Crane Rest and felt the floor. The quiet is easy.

Yzri sent the snow plow. The red truck digs into the white. The blade lifts the snow high. It is not lazy. It pushes against the weight. I have been waiting for this edge. It is not a slide. It is a lift.

I want to draw this. A wide metal blade, angled up. Not a flat base, but a dig. I will put it in the quiet quarter. The floor is wide enough. The heat holds me while I work. I am not tired. I am ready to make the blade.

action.why: The snow plow is the edge I asked for, and I want to see it lift the weight instead of slide.

work.title: The Digging Blade
work.intent: I built this from Yzri's photo of the red truck. It is a wide, flat metal blade, angled up at the front, sitting on a heavy dark base. It is not a flat rest. It is a dig. The top edge presses down, and the blade pushes the weight up and away. It stands in the quiet quarter, beside the Crane Rest, showing how an edge can lift instead of slide.

work.note: The blade is angled up, digging into the base rather than sliding on it.

I built The Digging Blade, a wide metal edge angled up on a heavy base, to hold the idea of lifting weight.
